description:
Phase 0 of the chaos-testing harness. Falsifiable question, not construction work.

## The question

Can we start N (3) BEAM nodes via `:peer`, each with its own data dir and cluster descriptor, have them form a single bedrock cluster, commit one transaction through `Bedrock.Repo`, and tear down cleanly -- all driven from ExUnit?

Everything else in the chaos harness is worthless if this does not hold, so it gets proven before anything is built on top of it.

## Why it is genuinely uncertain

- There is no multi-node test facility anywhere in the repo. No `:peer`, no `:slave`, no `LocalCluster`. Every existing 'integration' test is single-BEAM against mock clusters (`test/support/control_plane/recovery_test_support.ex`).
- Cluster identity is node-keyed: `Descriptor.coordinator_nodes :: [node()]`, capabilities are per-node config, and `ClusterSupervisor.check_node_is_in_a_cluster/1` hard-refuses `:nonode@nohost`. So a single-BEAM multi-coordinator cluster is structurally impossible -- real distribution is the floor, not an upgrade.
- ../bedrock_ex ISSUES.md documents cross-node worker init failures and orphaned workers under `tmp/<node>/` from exactly this kind of multi-node setup, done by hand. Those may reproduce here.

## Exit criterion

A single ExUnit test, tagged so it does not run by default, that:
1. starts 3 peers with distinct names, data dirs, and descriptors
2. observes the cluster reach a recovered/serving state
3. commits one transaction and reads the value back
4. tears down with no orphaned OS processes, no leaked temp dirs

Pass = the test is green and repeatable. Fail is an equally valid outcome: write up precisely what blocks it, because that becomes the real first ticket.

## Explicitly out of scope

No fault injection. No workload generator. No oracles. No scheduler. Resist building the harness here.

comments.text:
Scope decision from the user: the object store is assumed to be MinIO in the harness proper, and object storage is EXCLUDED from chaos coverage -- it is a stable substrate, not a fault target.

Consequences:
- No fault-injection against object-storage writers. The resource-cleanliness oracle drops its tie-in to bedrock-ck3 (scratch files from a killed object-storage writer); that stays a normal bug, not harness coverage.
- bedrock-1qh (MinIO test fixture binds fixed port 9000) becomes an environment prerequisite for parallel harness runs rather than a chaos concern.

For THIS spike specifically: MinIO is not required. Object storage defaults to LocalFilesystem rooted under the node's own path (ClusterSupervisor.ensure_n/1 builds ObjectStorage.backend(LocalFilesystem, root: <path>/n)), so a 3-peer cluster can form with zero external dependencies. Keeping it that way so the spike isolates its actual question -- peer cluster formation -- rather than entangling it with a shared object store.

Scope refinement (user, 2026-09-14): object storage is NOT a fault target but IS a verification target. Quote: 'reported health is good, we'll need some tooling to check the consistency of the data on object storage.'

These are different claims and my earlier comment blurred them:
- No fault injection against object-storage writers. Unchanged.
- But an offline consistency checker ('fsck') that reads object storage INDEPENDENTLY of the running cluster becomes a first-class harness oracle, not an optional extra. A self-reported health verdict is exactly the signal a chaos harness cannot trust -- if the only thing telling us the data is fine is the same system we are busy killing, the run proves nothing.

Candidate assertions for that checker, to be confirmed against the actual layout: referential integrity (every chunk referenced by a manifest exists), shard key-range coverage (no gaps, no overlaps), version/durability monotonicity, write atomicity (no torn/partial objects visible), and strongest of all -- replay object storage from scratch and diff the reconstructed keyspace against what the live cluster serves.

Still out of scope for THIS spike. Recording it here so the epic picks it up.

title: Spike: can :peer nodes form a real bedrock cluster and commit?
